releases.title: A first step onto the Secure Net protocol (experimental)
notes: Commonveil now carries the new Secure Net protocol (0.5.0) and takes its first step onto it. It is off unless you turn it on: Settings, Devices and keys, Experimental: Secure Net protocol.

With it on for both people, a direct message is sealed a second time under a one-off key. That key goes only to the devices linked at that moment, over post-quantum sessions (X25519 with ML-KEM-768), so someone who later gets hold of an account's keys or recovery phrase still can't read it.
It adds to the protection messages already have and never replaces it. Messages to people who haven't turned it on go exactly as before, and everything already sent stays readable.
Turning it on gives your account a protocol identity: a quantum-resistant key and the handle @username@site.

Limits for now: direct messages only (not groups, servers, edits, reactions or scheduled messages); a device added later can't read messages sent with it before; it can't be used together with a passcode lock; and it works within one site.
It is labelled experimental because the protocol has not had an independent security review yet. docs/SECURE_NET_LAYER.md says exactly what it does and what the site can see.
Self-hosted sites get the same feature with this update; there is nothing new to configure.

releases.title: A sealed, quantum-resistant relay between sites
notes: What one site sends another is now sealed for that site alone, so nothing in between can see who is writing to whom, which conversation, or what was asked: not the network, not a CDN or hosting platform, and not someone recording traffic to decrypt later.
The sealing is quantum-resistant: ML-KEM-768 together with a classical exchange, so it holds unless both are broken. Answers come back sealed too.
Sites sign what they send twice, with Ed25519 and the post-quantum ML-DSA-65. Both must check out.
A site that has started sealing can't be talked back down: other sites refuse it if its relay keys change or vanish, and refuse plain or singly-signed requests from it.
Communities' signed records (history, votes, results) can use quantum-resistant keys.
Your messages themselves were already quantum-resistant end to end. Still classical for now: the signatures your devices put on messages, and private voting tokens.
Built on Secure Net 0.3.1. Self-hosted sites pick this up by updating; nothing to configure.

releases.title: The hosted site can talk to self-hosted sites
notes: The hosted site now speaks the same protocol as self-hosted sites: people on either can find each other by address, start conversations, and read and reply, end-to-end encrypted, with each person's keys checked against their own key history.

Sites now tell each other where their protocol endpoints are in their site document, so a site that can only be reached under a path can take part. Self-hosted sites need this release to talk to the hosted site.
People from other sites never get an account on the hosted site: it keeps only what their own site shares about them, and they can't sign in there.
Not yet between the hosted site and others: calls and presence, files and pictures in conversations hosted elsewhere, and holding messages for a site that's down.
Self-hosted sites: new optional setting FEDERATION_PATH_PREFIX, for a site that can only be reached under a path.
Built on Secure Net 0.2.1.

releases.title: A full security review, and Secure Net
notes: All 24 findings from an independent security review are fixed, each with a test. docs/SECURITY_REVIEW.md lists them.
Disconnecting a device, changing your password or recovering your account now signs out every other session at once.
Adding a passkey, approving a new browser or replacing your owner key now needs proof it's you: one of your devices confirms it without asking, or you enter your password.
Removing a device now changes the keys of every community it could read, so it can't read anything new.
Self-hosted sites: the first admin needs a one-time setup code printed on the server, so a stranger can't claim a new site first. ADMIN_USERNAMES and email (SMTP) settings are gone.
Self-hosted sites: updates that fail no longer stay "Updating…", the updater won't go backwards unless you allow it, and backups are pruned by age.
Self-hosted sites no longer depend on Base44 in any way: the image builds and runs with nothing of theirs, and a check stops the build if that ever changes.
Talking to other sites is safer: a site's address is checked at the moment of connecting, and replies are cut off as soon as they're too big.

Commonveil is now built on Secure Net, our protocol as a separate library (github.com/Comutability/secure-net) that other apps and sites can use. It adds communities that approved sites can mirror and keep running if their home site goes down, structured debates and votes (public or secret) that can authorise changes, private tokens (RFC 9497), personas, consent capsules, and extension and theme manifests.

releases.title: Sign in your way, install the app, and private push notifications
notes: New accounts are a username and password, on every Commonveil site. No email needed.
Accounts made with an email before today still sign in with it, and can add a username and password, or a passkey, and then remove the email.
Joining asks you to confirm you're 16 or older. Accounts found to belong to someone younger are closed.
Terms of Use, in plain language, linked from sign-up and every page.
Install Commonveil as an app on your phone, tablet or computer: its own icon and window, opening straight to your messages, still this website with no app store.

Push notifications, off until you turn them on. They say only "New message", never who it's from, which conversation or what was said, so your phone and its push service keep no record. Tapping one opens the right conversation.
Better for screen readers and keyboards: a skip link in the app, clearer names for buttons and badges, and higher-contrast avatars.

Easier to find: every page that works without signing in has its own title, description and link preview, with a sitemap for search engines. The app is never indexed, and nor are invites, reset links or people's profiles.
New Help Centre article: installing the app. The notifications article now covers push.

releases.title: Offline mode
notes: Keep writing with no connection: each message is encrypted and signed on your device straight away, waits there, and goes out when you're back, showing the time you wrote it.
Offline mode in settings stops the app reaching the server until you turn it off. Everything you send in the meantime waits, already encrypted.
If something changed while you were away, a waiting message is marked "Not sent", with Send again or Delete.
Self-hosted sites hold messages for other sites they can't reach, and pass them on when they can, for up to a week.
A self-hosted site can run on a small computer with its own Wi-Fi, so people nearby can chat with no internet. The guide is in docs/OFFLINE.md and docs/SELF_HOSTING.md.
New Help Centre articles: offline mode, people on other sites, sign-in and recovery, and running your own site.

releases.title: Commonveil Identity
notes: On self-hosted sites, accounts are a username and password, with no email.
Sign in with a passkey, kept on one device or synced by a password manager.

A browser signing in for the first time is confirmed with a passkey, your recovery phrase or private key, or from a device you're already signed in on. Signed-in devices are listed in settings, where you can disconnect any of them.
Your private key is your recovery phrase written as one string: either proves the account is yours. Getting back in takes one of them, or a passkey.
Accounts made with an email still work, and are asked to add a passkey and confirm their phrase before email sign-in goes away.

releases.title: Run it yourself, and talk across sites
notes: Commonveil can run on your own hardware with Docker, without Base44: one install script, HTTPS included.
Self-hosted sites show admins when a new release is out, with an update button, and can update themselves automatically. Each update is backed up first and undone if it doesn't start.

Self-hosted sites talk to each other with the Commonveil Protocol: everyone has an address like @ann.chat.example.com that also opens their profile, and conversations and servers work across sites, still end-to-end encrypted.
Browse and join servers listed on other sites from Discover.
Profile pictures.
The message box grows with longer messages, and can be expanded.
The home page compares Commonveil with other privacy-focused chat apps.

releases.title: A tighter site, with release notes
notes: Guides, learning paths, the wiki and the blog have been removed, so the site is about Commonveil itself. Their old addresses now lead to the Help Centre.
Release notes for every version, from 0.1.0 onwards, on the site and as tags on GitHub.
The site's version is shown at the bottom of every page.
Commonveil is now free software, under the AGPL-3.0.

releases.title: Help Centre
notes: A Help Centre with an article for every feature: what it's for, how to use it and what it shares.
The complete guide on one page, to print or download, and as docs/USER_GUIDE.md on GitHub.
"How this works" links from settings pages to the right article.

releases.title: Scheduled tasks fixed
notes: Scheduled tasks now run reliably: scheduled messages, check-ins and self-destructing conversations every 5 minutes, disappearing messages every 30 minutes, and opt-in account deletion daily.
The self-destruct menu no longer lists "Off" twice.

releases.title: Send later, safety check-ins and self-destructing chats
notes: Send later: write now, deliver from a minute to a year ahead.
Safety check-ins: a message that sends itself unless you tap "I'm OK" in time.
Self-destructing conversations, deleted for everyone at a time you choose.
A privacy report showing everything the service holds about you, with a privacy checkup.
Quiet hours and focus for notifications, kept on your device.

releases.title: Names in moderation
notes: Reports and cases show the names of members who aren't in the member list, instead of "Member".

releases.title: Security audit and built-in moderation
notes: Fixes from a full security review: channel permissions, private channels, call membership checks and safer word matching.
Reports to a server's moderators, encrypted to them alone, and escalation to the Commonveil team.
Numbered cases, warnings with automatic steps, flood and raid protection, staff limits, temporary bans and message purges.

releases.title: Files, voice messages, events and more
notes: Encrypted files and voice messages.
A server's own emoji and stickers, AutoMod, threads and events.
Optional online status and typing, stage channels, and calls in conversations.

releases.title: Video and screen sharing
notes: Turn your camera on or share your screen in calls, with every video frame encrypted too.

releases.title: Polls, inbox and quick switcher
notes: Polls, every emoji as a reaction, an inbox for mentions and unread channels, saved messages, a quick switcher (Ctrl + K), server folders, private notes and forwarding.

releases.title: Calls recover from network drops
notes: Calls find a new route by themselves after a network drop.

releases.title: Calls survive a quick reconnect
notes: You keep your place in a call through a quick reconnect.

releases.title: Encrypted voice calls
notes: Peer-to-peer voice calls in voice channels, with signed connections and every audio frame encrypted with the channel's keys.

releases.title: Server settings fixes
notes: Server settings load correctly after a reload, a note about staff in member lists, and clearer text while waiting for keys.

releases.title: Servers and the community hub
notes: Encrypted servers with channels, roles, invites and Discover, the Commonveil Community server, and post-quantum hybrid keys, now live.

releases.title: Faster server updates
notes: Server changes are checked separately from messages.

releases.title: A new layout
notes: A server rail, channel list, chat, forums, tickets and settings, laid out like Discord.

releases.title: Who hands out keys
notes: Servers choose whether any member's app or only staff hand keys to newcomers.

releases.title: Post-quantum keys and encrypted servers
notes: Keys sealed with ML-KEM-768 and P-256 together, and the groundwork for encrypted servers.

releases.title: Checks after going live
notes: The live site was checked, and the security policy test fixed.

releases.title: Live, with updated privacy pages
notes: The new features were verified on the live site, and the Privacy and Security pages updated.

releases.title: Replies, reactions and a passcode lock
notes: Replies, reactions and edits; disappearing-message timers and group admins; alerts; message search on your device; a passcode lock; a download of your data; opt-in auto-delete; and site search.

releases.title: Timers, admins and security emails
notes: Disappearing messages, group admins, security emails, opt-in deletion of unused accounts and scheduled clean-up, on the server.

releases.title: Protocol version 2
notes: Fixes from a review of the encryption protocol, each member reading with their own access, and a staff tool for erasing what removed sign-ins left behind.

releases.title: Signed group changes
notes: Changes to groups need a device signature, membership can be paused, a stale-keys fix, and a browser test suite.

releases.title: The rebuild
notes: Commonveil rebuilt from scratch: end-to-end encrypted direct messages and groups, device linking, a 24-word recovery phrase and safety numbers.
The public site, with content brought over from the old one.
